strongest_opponent_point: Trend-follower owns the only seat that is opposite on both USD and CAD, and the only attack that actually hits a live leg of short CA-US_2Y: US 2Y is higher on every frozen horizon (+9bp 1d, +13bp 5d, +57bp 1m and 3m, 99.8th percentile 1y as of 2026-09-18) after a delivered 25bp hike that was already >90% priced, so receiving the US 2Y leg is a premature fade of a still-rising front end; they also read the 1m USDCAD bounce (+1.74% to 1.401047) as CAD lower. That is the claim that can cheapen CA-US through the US side without any Canada confirmation.
holes_in_opposing_case: FACT: the USD-higher coalition is not a CAD/USD argument. Dollar-king marks cad_view neutral and explicitly refuses long USDCAD because WTI 107.02 (96.4th percentile, +24.2% 1m) and CA activity 53.2 / consumer 52.5 support CAD; their USD higher is short AUDUSD on AU housing/labor. Perma-bear and rate-dove also map AU stamp-duty -24% y/y, volumes -18%, AU labor 47.8 and AU 2Y at a 99th-percentile 4.999 into USD higher with CAD not_relevant. An Australian housing break does not justify a 140bp Canada policy discount versus the US.

FACT: trend-follower’s CAD-lower tag is not their trade. They rejected long USDCAD because the 3m return is still -1.25% with 1y z 0.80 / ~74th percentile. Inferring CAD lower from a 1m-only +1.74% bounce against a still-negative 3m print is the premature trend they accuse others of running. USDCAD (1y 74.0th / 5y 87.0th) is not remotely as stretched as CA-US_2Y at -140.0bp (1y 3.77th / 5y 4.31st, z_1y -1.84).

FACT/INFERENCE: treating the already-extreme CA-US gap as ‘secondary confirmation’ that it should cheapen further is trend-chasing a tail. CA 2Y itself is 3.27 at a 97.8th percentile 1y after +31bp 1m — Canada has not been easing in absolute terms; it has merely lagged a US 2Y that packed +57bp into a hike that was already priced. The 17 Sep CA 2Y -8bp dip is one session, not a BoC path.
FACT: broad USD is stale as of 2026-09-11 at 118.21, 11.9th percentile, z -1.33, 3m -1.60%. Pair-wise USD higher versus AUD does not generalize to a USD-higher regime versus CAD.

Catalyst-junkie, rate-hawk, value-guy and cross-merchant are also routed here while already owning CAD higher / Canada re-rate; conflict count overstates disagreement on the Canada expression.

FACT: risk internals contradict mapping the Fed hike into USD higher / CAD lower. HY OAS 270bp is a 13.7th percentile; VIX 15.44 is a 14.7th percentile; copper futures closed 6.7155 at a 99.2nd percentile. Dollar-king even concedes VIX at the 15th percentile is a risk-on tape. That is cyclical adaptation, not a flight-to-USD that should keep Canada 140bp cheap.
attack: USD higher as a blanket tag is an Australia story wearing a dollar label. The dedicated USD seat will not express it in USDCAD, and the AU duration seats leave CAD unpriced. That coalition cannot be used to veto a Canada-versus-US 2Y that sits at a dual-horizon cheap tail.

CAD lower is a one-seat inference from a 1-month USDCAD bounce that the same seat would not trade. Three-month USDCAD is still down, CFTC CAD shorts are covering, WTI is at a 96th percentile, and BoC minutes flag energy pass-through against headline CPI still 3.0% with core near 2%. That is not a CAD-down tape.

Paying US 2Y at a 1y extreme after a pre-priced hike is not required to keep Canada 140bp easier. US activity 49.92 and consumer 48.5 (Michigan preliminary September 47.8) versus Canada activity 53.2, consumer 52.5 and Q2 GDP +0.8% q/q is the cyclical ranking in the packet. If US 2Y keeps rising, the RV still works if CA 2Y catches up; outright short US 2Y needs the continuation and fights coupon. Short CA-US_2Y receives 4.76 versus pays 3.27.

Spot long CAD is the inferior cousin the USD-higher camp wants to debate. USDCAD carry of 140bp opposes long CAD; the same 140bp supports short CA-US_2Y. Rates-first and the frozen stretch both keep the trade in the spread, not in the FX print.
defense: FACT: CA-US_2Y remains the cleanest pro-cyclical expression in the packet. Canada leads activity and consumer gauges; the spread is a 1y 3.77th / 5y 4.31st percentile after cheapening about 17bp over one month; HY, VIX and copper say the growth regime is adapting through the hike and the energy shock. INFERENCE: markets are still pricing Canada as if it needs ~140bp easier policy than a Fed that has already delivered. UNKNOWN: the frozen RV mark is 2026-09-17 while US 2Y printed +9bp on 2026-09-18, so the live spread may already be a few basis points more negative; NZ official yields and CME FX positioning are unavailable.

The receive-US leg is not a z-score fade of US 2Y in isolation. It is the other side of a relative Canada cheapness that CA 2Y at a 97.8th percentile 1y has not closed. Mean-reverter’s outright receive-US_2Y is the same US overshoot without the Canada catch-up; rate-hawk’s short CA-US_2Y is the same RV with both legs higher. Neither refutes paying CA versus receiving US.

expression_comparison.rationale: The mispricing lives in the policy differential, not in the FX print. CA-US 2Y is -140.0 bps at a 1y 3.77th percentile and 5y 4.31st percentile after cheapening about 17bp over one month; USDCAD is only a 1y 74th percentile and a 5y 87th percentile, so CAD weakness versus USD is not comparably extreme. Packet carry ranks USDCAD as long-USD/short-CAD on a 140bp 2Y differential, so spot long-CAD fights carry, whereas short CA-US_2Y receives the higher US 2Y and pays the lower CA 2Y. Rates-first mandate prefers this when both expressions are executable; both marks exist. Round 2 does not change the comparison: the USD-higher camp will not own USDCAD, and the CAD-lower seat rejected it as a weaker, 1-month-only trend versus a still-negative 3m USDCAD print.

revised_trade.structure: Pay Canada 2Y versus receive US 2Y; paper instrument CA-US_2Y, side short.
revised_trade.thesis: FACT: Canada activity temperature is 53.2 and consumer 52.5, the highest of the four countries; Q2 real GDP was +0.8% q/q versus a revised +0.1% in Q1; August headline CPI held at 3.0% with CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%; BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk. FACT: The Fed raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00% after futures entered the decision with >90% hike odds; US 2Y is 4.76 (1y 99.8th percentile, +57bp over one month) and US 10Y is 5.01. FACT: CA 2Y is 3.27 versus US 2Y 4.76; CA-US_2Y is -140.0 bps (1y percentile 3.77, 5y percentile 4.31, z_1y -1.84, z_5y -1.51), cheaper by about 17bp over one month. FACT: HY OAS is 270bp (1y 13.7th percentile), VIX is 15.44 (1y 14.7th percentile), copper futures closed 6.7155 (1y 99.2nd percentile), and Saudi ship-to-ship crude via Oman reduced the extreme oil-supply tail. INFERENCE: Markets are pricing Canada as if it needs ~140bp easier policy than the US despite Canada being the cyclical leader and carrying an explicit energy-inflation risk; that is defensive Canada pricing, not a growth-break. Risk-on internals (tight credit, low vol, high copper) say the global expansion is adapting through the hike and the energy shock. The cleanest pro-cyclical expression is therefore relative Canada rate cheapness versus the US, not a crowded AUD (housing slump; AUDCAD 1y/5y ~99.8th percentile) and not long CAD spot, which pays the same 140bp the wrong way. UNKNOWN: NZ official yields are unavailable so NZ rate RV cannot confirm a broader commodity-bloc catch-up; CME FX positioning is unavailable; CA-US_2Y is dated 2026-09-17 while US 2Y printed +9bp on 2026-09-18, so the live spread may already be a few basis points more negative than the frozen mark.
revised_trade.mispricing: Canada 2Y trades 140bp through US 2Y at a 1y 3.77th / 5y 4.31st percentile even though Canada has the strongest activity and consumer gauges and the BoC has flagged energy pass-through. The closing mechanism is Canada yields rising relative to the US (BoC forced to respect growth plus energy) and/or the US front end, already at a 1y extreme after a delivered hike, failing to cheapen as much as the 140bp Canada discount implies.
why_now: Fed just delivered the already-priced 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% and US 2Y is at a 1y 99.8th percentile, so the receive-US side of the pair is not waiting on a hawkish surprise.
CA-US 2Y cheapened about 17bp over one month to a 1y extreme of -140.0 bps while Canada still leads on activity 53.2 and consumer 52.5.
BoC energy pass-through risk is live against Brent 130.8 on 2026-09-15; the Saudi Oman workaround cut the tail but did not erase Canadian inflation risk.
HY OAS 270bp and VIX 15.44 show financial stress is not the binding constraint; copper at a 99th percentile close supports a cyclical, not recession, regime.

The 13 funded seats pay 5% ACT/365 on the full $100m whether deployed or not; receiving 4.76% versus paying 3.27% is a 140bp running differential that works with the clock, unlike sitting flat or buying CAD spot.
